blocks.source: 张巍GRE填空机经2000题 · Test 137 Section 1
blocks.noteTail: （原题及配套答案，仅供个人学习；暂不附讲解）

stem: Historians of medicine are resigned to doctors’ ____ medical history: physicians offer hagiographic biographies of obscure nineteenth-century medical figures, triumphalist narratives of medical progress, and retrospective diagnoses of ailments afflicting historical characters.
Reports of the destruction of island vegetation by human-introduced herbivores, such as goats and rabbits, are so (i)____ that there can be no reason to (ii)____.
colsZh: 悲惨的；不吉利的；恐怖的

stem: George Eliot's biographer can be highly inventive, but, at the same time, somewhat (i)____ in her approach to Eliot. She will hoist an alluring psychological flag concerning Eliot and then scrupulously take it down again, because the evidence will not serve to (ii)____ it. But she takes it down only after it has taken an entirely (iii)____ flutter in the breeze.
colsZh: （时常伴有夸张和想象内容地）详细说明
有正当理由的；被证明合理的

stem: The museum’s display of bandolier bags made by Ojibwa artists of the Mille Lacs community reinforces the idea that this community’s culture is ____ one: early twentieth-century bandolier bags are displayed alongside others made recently.
At the core of science fiction is the notion of ____, of asking, "If this phenomenon continues, where will it lead?"
optsZh: 外推；依据已知信息推断

stem: Certainly, the drive to make safety a corporate priority is ____, but whether it will be enough to create the necessary change in corporate culture is another matter; organizational inertia can be a powerful force.
optsZh: 批评的，批判的；紧要的，关键性的；严重的，危急的

stem: The idea that Antarctica’s subglacial lakes are ____ has changed radically thanks to repeat- pass satellite altimetry technology, which has found evidence of water transfer between lakes at distances of more than 200 kilometers.
